message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"8.1","text":"As Peter was entering Tripolis, many of those more eager to learn, from Tyre and Sidon as well as Beirut and Byblos and the neighboring districts, were entering with him. Especially, too, crowds from the city itself were converging, wishing to question him. So in the suburbs we were met by the brothers whom he had sent out to ascertain precisely both the other matters concerning the city and what Simon was doing, so that they might return and give an account. They welcomed him and led him to the house of Maroones.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"οἱ φιλομαθέστεροι","chosen":"those more eager to learn","rationale":"The comparative describes people especially fond of learning; “the more inquisitive” is also possible."},{"source_quote":"ἱστορεῖν βουλομένων αὐτόν","chosen":"wishing to question him","rationale":"ἱστορεῖν with a personal object can mean to inquire of or question someone, rather than merely to learn about that person."},{"source_quote":"τὰ πραττόμενα τῷ Σίμωνι","chosen":"what Simon was doing","rationale":"The dative may denote Simon's activities or affairs; “what was happening with Simon” is a viable broader rendering."},{"source_quote":"ὅπως ἐλθόντες ὑφηγήσωνται","chosen":"so that they might return and give an account","rationale":"The motion is understood contextually as coming back to Peter after their fact-finding mission; more literally, “so that, having come, they might explain.”"},{"source_quote":"τὴν Μαροόνου ... οἰκίαν","chosen":"the house of Maroones","rationale":"Μαροόνου is treated as the genitive of the personal name Μαροόνης, transliterated Maroones."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"8.2","text":"When he had already reached the very gate of the guesthouse, he turned to the crowds and promised to speak with them about reverence for God after the coming night. When he entered, the advance party prepared lodging for those who had gathered. Nor did those who received and hosted them fall short of the eagerness of those asking to host them. Peter knew nothing of these arrangements, and when we invited him to partake of food, he said that he himself would not partake before those who had assembled for him had found rest. We answered, “This has already been accomplished as follows: making their affection for you their plea, people received all of them with such eagerness that those who had obtained no one to host were exceedingly grieved.” When Peter heard this, he was delighted; and after blessing them for their prompt kindness, he went out, bathed in the sea, came back inside, partook of food with the advance party, and, as evening came on, went to sleep.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἐπ’ αὐτῷ τῷ τῆς ξενίας πυλῶνι","chosen":"at the very gate of the guesthouse","rationale":"ξενία can denote hospitality, lodging, or guest quarters; the mention of a gate favors a place of lodging."},{"source_quote":"μετὰ τὴν ἐπιοῦσαν","chosen":"after the coming night","rationale":"The feminine adjective has an omitted noun. Although ἡ ἐπιοῦσα often means “the following day,” the subsequent evening, sleep, and expectation of an address “today” favor understanding an ensuing night here."},{"source_quote":"οἱ πρόοδοι","chosen":"the advance party","rationale":"The noun denotes those sent ahead, identified later as the twelve who had gone in advance."},{"source_quote":"τῆς τῶν ἀξιούντων προθυμίας","chosen":"the eagerness of those asking to host them","rationale":"ἀξιούντων may refer to people making a request; the later grief of those without guests supports understanding the request as one to provide hospitality. “Those who considered it an honor” remains possible."},{"source_quote":"προφάσει τῆς πρὸς σὲ στοργῆς","chosen":"making their affection for you their plea","rationale":"πρόφασις can mean a pretext, plea, or stated reason; “plea” preserves the expressed motive without necessarily implying insincerity."},{"source_quote":"τῆς ὀξείας φιλανθρωπίας","chosen":"for their prompt kindness","rationale":"Literally “keen” or “swift benevolence”; the context emphasizes the speed and eagerness of their hospitality."},{"source_quote":"ἑσπέρας ἐπικαταλαβούσης ὕπνωσεν","chosen":"as evening came on, went to sleep","rationale":"The image is of evening overtaking or coming upon the situation; idiomatic English uses “came on.”"}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"μετὰ τὴν ἐπιοῦσαν","issue":"The omitted noun creates a genuine temporal ambiguity. Supplying the conventional ἡμέραν gives “after the following day,” while the narrative sequence supports supplying νύκτα, “after the coming night.” No textual alteration is proposed.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"8.3","text":"At about the second crowing of the roosters, he awoke and found us awake. All of us with him numbered sixteen: Peter himself, I, Clement, Nicetas and Aquila, and the twelve who had gone ahead. After greeting us, he said, “Today, since we are not devoting our time to those outside, we are free for one another. Therefore I will recount to you what happened after the departure from Tyre, and you tell me what Simon has done here and explain it in greater detail.” After we had exchanged our accounts in turn, one of our companions came in and reported to Peter, “Simon, having learned that you had arrived, set out on the road toward Syria. The crowds have regarded this one night as a year's span and are unable to wait for the time appointed by you. They are standing before the doors in clusters and gatherings, talking with one another about Simon's slander. They say that after raising their expectations and promising that, when you came, he would expose you as guilty of many evils, he learned that you had arrived and fled by night. But as they long to hear you, a certain rumor—I do not know from where—has fallen upon them that you are going to speak with them today. Therefore, so that they do not wear themselves out for a long time only to disperse to no purpose, you yourself know what you ought to do.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ὑπὸ δὲ τὰς δευτέρας τῶν ἀλεκτρυόνων φωνὰς","chosen":"At about the second crowing of the roosters","rationale":"The plural phrase refers to the second cockcrow or round of rooster calls; ὑπό here marks approximate time."},{"source_quote":"τοῖς ἔξω μὴ σχολάζοντες","chosen":"since we are not devoting our time to those outside","rationale":"σχολάζω with the dative means to be occupied with or devote time to someone; τοῖς ἔξω may mean outsiders generally or, in context, the people physically outside."},{"source_quote":"ἀμειψαμένων οὖν ἀλλήλους ταῖς ἐν μέρει διηγήσεσιν","chosen":"After we had exchanged our accounts in turn","rationale":"ἐν μέρει indicates narration by turns, with each side giving its account."},{"source_quote":"τὴν ἐπὶ Συρίαν ὥρμησεν ὁδόν","chosen":"set out on the road toward Syria","rationale":"ἐπί with the accusative expresses direction toward Syria; ὁρμάω conveys setting out energetically."},{"source_quote":"τῆς τοῦ Σίμωνος διαβολῆς","chosen":"Simon's slander","rationale":"διαβολή can mean slander, accusation, or calumny; the ensuing claim against Peter supports “slander.”"},{"source_quote":"μετεωρίσας αὐτοὺς","chosen":"raising their expectations","rationale":"μετεωρίζω can mean to lift up, excite, or keep in suspense; the promised confrontation has heightened their expectations."},{"source_quote":"ἐπὶ πολλοῖς κακοῖς σε ἐλέγξειν","chosen":"expose you as guilty of many evils","rationale":"ἐλέγχειν may mean expose, convict, or refute, while ἐπὶ πολλοῖς κακοῖς states the alleged wrongs on which the exposure would rest."},{"source_quote":"φήμη τις ἐπέπεσεν","chosen":"a certain rumor ... has fallen upon them","rationale":"The wording preserves the source's image of a rumor falling upon or overtaking the crowd; “has reached them” would be more idiomatic."},{"source_quote":"ἀλόγως διαλύωνται","chosen":"disperse to no purpose","rationale":"ἀλόγως can mean unreasonably, pointlessly, or without due cause; the concern is that their prolonged waiting might prove futile."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"τοῦ-Σίμωνος","issue":"The hyphen between the article and the name has no syntactic or lexical function and is treated as an editorial or line-division feature rather than as part of the name.","proposed_reading":"τοῦ Σίμωνος","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"8.4","text":"And Peter, marveling at the crowds' eagerness, answered, “See, brothers, how our Lord's words are visibly being fulfilled. For I remember him saying, ‘Many will come from east and west, north and south, and will recline in the bosoms of Abraham and Isaac and Jacob.’ But he also says, ‘Many are called, but few are chosen.’ Thus the part about their coming when called has been fulfilled. But since this is not their own doing, but God's—‘the one who called’ them and caused them to come—they have no reward for this alone, because it is not their own doing but belongs to the one who brought it about. But if, after being called, they do good deeds, which is their own doing, then they will have a reward for this.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"οἱ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν λόγοι ἐμφανῶς τελοῦνται","chosen":"our Lord's words are visibly being fulfilled","rationale":"τελοῦνται denotes being accomplished or fulfilled, while ἐμφανῶς stresses that the fulfillment is evident."},{"source_quote":"ἄρκτου τε καὶ μεσημβρίας","chosen":"north and south","rationale":"ἄρκτος, literally “the Bear,” denotes the north, while μεσημβρία, literally “midday,” denotes the south."},{"source_quote":"ἀνακλιθήσονται εἰς κόλπους","chosen":"will recline in the bosoms","rationale":"The rendering preserves both the banquet image of reclining and the unusual plural κόλπους; “at the breastsides” or “in the embraces” would interpret the image more strongly."},{"source_quote":"τὸ μὲν οὖν ἐλθεῖν αὐτοὺς κληθέντας πεπλήρωται","chosen":"the part about their coming when called has been fulfilled","rationale":"The articular infinitive identifies their coming in response to being called as the element already fulfilled."},{"source_quote":"οὐκ αὐτῶν ἐστὶν τοῦτο ἴδιον","chosen":"this is not their own doing","rationale":"ἴδιον marks what belongs distinctively to them; “doing” fits the contrast with God's action and their later good deeds."},{"source_quote":"τοῦ καλέσαντος","chosen":"the one who called","rationale":"The source itself marks this phrase as a quotation, so the quotation is retained rather than absorbed into the surrounding clause."},{"source_quote":"τοῦ ἐνεργήσαντος","chosen":"the one who brought it about","rationale":"ἐνεργέω here refers to the agent who effected their coming, not merely one who was active in a general sense."},{"source_quote":"καλὰ πράξωσιν","chosen":"do good deeds","rationale":"The phrase refers to performing morally good actions, in contrast with merely responding to the divine call."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"8.5","text":"“For not even Hebrews who believe Moses while not keeping what was said through him are saved, unless they keep what was said to them. For even the fact that they believed Moses did not arise from their own decision, but from God, who said to Moses, ‘Look, I myself am coming to you in a pillar of cloud, so that the people may hear me speaking to you and may believe you forever.’ Therefore, since for both Hebrews and those called from the nations, believing teachers of truth has come from God, while good deeds have been left to each person to perform according to that person's own judgment, the reward is rightly paid to those who do good. For there would have been no need either for Moses or for Jesus's coming, if indeed they were willing to understand what is reasonable on their own; nor does salvation come about by believing teachers and calling them lords.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τὰ δι’ αὐτοῦ ῥηθέντα μὴ φυλάσσοντες","chosen":"while not keeping what was said through him","rationale":"φυλάσσω here means to observe or obey what was spoken, while διά presents Moses as the one through whom it was communicated."},{"source_quote":"τὸ Μωϋσεῖ πιστεῦσαι αὐτοὺς","chosen":"the fact that they believed Moses","rationale":"The articular infinitive makes their belief in Moses the subject of the clause; πιστεύω with the dative can mean believe or trust someone."},{"source_quote":"οὐχὶ τῆς αὐτῶν βουλῆς γέγονεν","chosen":"did not arise from their own decision","rationale":"βουλή may mean counsel, purpose, or decision; “decision” best expresses the contrast with God's initiative."},{"source_quote":"ἐν στύλῳ νεφέλης","chosen":"in a pillar of cloud","rationale":"The wording specifically presents a pillar of cloud and is not replaced by a more familiar rendering from another textual form."},{"source_quote":"τοῖς ἀπὸ ἐθνῶν κεκλημένοις","chosen":"those called from the nations","rationale":"The phrase identifies people called from among the nations; “Gentiles who were called” is a viable idiomatic alternative."},{"source_quote":"τὸ διδασκάλοις ἀληθείας πιστεῦσαι","chosen":"believing teachers of truth","rationale":"The dative construction denotes placing belief or trust in teachers characterized as teachers of truth."},{"source_quote":"τῶν καλῶν πράξεων ἰδίᾳ κρίσει ἑκάστῳ ποιεῖν ἀπολελειμμένων","chosen":"good deeds have been left to each person to perform according to that person's own judgment","rationale":"The construction contrasts divinely produced belief with actions left to each individual's κρίσις, which may also be rendered “choice” or “decision.”"},{"source_quote":"τῆς τοῦ Ἰησοῦ παρουσίας","chosen":"Jesus's coming","rationale":"παρουσία can denote presence, arrival, or coming; the contrast with the need for Moses favors Jesus's historical coming, though “the presence of Jesus” remains possible."},{"source_quote":"τὸ εὔλογον","chosen":"what is reasonable","rationale":"The adjective used substantivally denotes what accords with reason; “the reasonable course” is also possible."},{"source_quote":"κυρίους αὐτοὺς λέγειν","chosen":"calling them lords","rationale":"The plural κυρίους may mean lords or masters. “Lords” preserves the source's title-like wording and its application to the teachers under discussion."}],"source_issues":[]}]}
